newsitem.title: BERMUDA: Mid Ocean Q1 hurt by forex, drop in gains.
newsitem.headline: Mid Ocean Q1 hurt by forex, drop in gains.

text.p: Mid Ocean Ltd said first quarter results were hurt, in part, by reduced investment gains and increased foreign exchange losses as well as adverse adjustments to business written in prior years.

Mid Ocean earlier reported first quarter net fell to $1.43 a share compared to $1.57 a year ago. Operating earnings were $1.36 a share compared to $1.32 a share a year ago, but below Wall Street's consensus estimate of $1.42 a share.
But Mid Ocean chief executive Michael Butt said "profitability for the quarter remained much in line with our expectations as a result of favorable loss experience."
Premiums written came under pressure in the first quarter because of a highly competitive renewal season, Butt said.
Net premiums written fell to $250.1 million in the first quarter compared to $288.9 million a year ago.
"Our results reflect a highly competitive renewal season in virtually all lines we underwrite," he said.
"On the revenue front, this environment combined with our disciplined underwriting approach led to a decline in premiums written," he said.
Global market conditions, he said, are likely to remain competitive.

"Market conditions on a global basis appear as if they will remain highly competitive in most geographic areas and lines of business, although some appear better than others and this is where we intend to focus our activities," Butt said.
He said Mid Ocean also expects positive growth from its investment in the Brockbank Group, in part due to its decision to increase its dedicated underwriting capacity by about 40 percent this year.
